headline: OPENAI HIRED THE MAN WHO BUILT PATREON, AND ITS SPONSORED POSTS FOR CHATGPT WENT FROM 61 A MONTH TO 141
deck: Sam Yam co-founded Patreon thirteen years ago and ran its technology.  This morning he said he is joining OpenAI to lead Creator Product, and taking Patreon's former head of product and head of engineering with him.  Hours later Business Insider published the other half: OpenAI's sponsored creator posts for ChatGPT have more than doubled since June.  One company is now buying the pipe creators get paid through and the creators themselves.
tldr: OpenAI hired Patreon co-founder and technology chief Sam Yam to lead Creator Product, with Patreon's former heads of product and engineering joining him, and pointed at DevDay on 29 September — while its sponsored Instagram posts for ChatGPT went from 61 in June to 122 in July to 141 in August, per HypeAuditor.  Compare your current creator quotes in parenting, fitness and technology against June quotes, and move budget to a category OpenAI is not bidding in rather than matching a price set by a buyer with no cost per customer to defend.

Since 24 August YouTube counts a public view from the first frame rather than after about thirty seconds, and Agentio's measurement of more than 75,000 videos found public views overstating engaged views by 1.67 times on average — 85 percent on channels under 50,000 subscribers against 49 percent on channels over 300,000 — while earnings still run on engaged figures.  Write engaged views into your next creator contract as the reported metric and ask for a Studio screenshot showing both numbers side by side.

Bob's Discount Furniture reports 152 million views, 223 million impressions and nearly nine million dollars of attributed sales from its social reality series about couples choosing furniture, and has commissioned a second season, while four marketers told Digiday that scripted branded microdramas from Crocs, Nuuly and Native still have no business case.  Check that the purchase decision your customer makes appears on screen in every episode of anything you commission, and set the attribution method at commission rather than after.

Nielsen has YouTube at a record 14.2 percent of American television viewing time in July against Netflix on 7.8, with YouTube advertising revenue at 11.06 billion dollars in Alphabet's second quarter, up 13 percent, and both HSBC and Wells Fargo downgrading Netflix.  Take that chart into your budget meeting and ask what share of your video budget goes to the platform holding 14.2 percent of television time, then run a test against television benchmarks rather than social ones.

USA Fencing put twelve creators with more than 215 million combined followers against four Team USA fencers this week and pointed the whole thing at TryFencing.org, where 800 clubs had already agreed standing trial offers, against a creator programme baseline of 4.75 million impressions a month.  Build and staff the single action you want viewers to take before you buy any reach, and count how many partners have agreed to it, because that number caps everything the campaign can deliver.

Snap's Ipsos study reporting that 42 percent of daily social media users watch short dramas daily screened every one of its 3,000 respondents to be a current watcher or someone interested in the format, and its competitive claim rests on a four-point gap, 32 percent against a 28 percent average.  Read the screening criteria on every platform study before the findings, and treat any adoption figure from a pre-screened sample as an upper bound in your deck.

TBPN did about five million dollars of advertising in 2025 and was reported on track for between 15 and 30 million in 2026 off a YouTube channel of roughly 58,000 subscribers at the time OpenAI bought it, with about 70,000 viewers per daily episode, and Sammi Cohen launches a copy of the format on 6 October.  If your customers are a defined professional group, price a weekly live show at a fixed hour before you price another campaign, and ask small shows for daily viewership and time of day rather than subscriber count.
